title: The Verb 'To Be'
subtitle: Eom, eart, is — the most irregular verb in the language.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of The Verb 'To Be'.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body: The verb 'to be' (bēon / wesan) is suppletive: it uses forms from two different roots. Present: eom, eart, is, sind/sindon/sint. Past: wæs, wǣre, wæs, wǣron. Infinitive: bēon (future-oriented) or wesan (present-oriented). Essential, irregular, everywhere.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Ic eom cyning (I am king). Hē wæs cyning (He was king).

items.answer: Review the paradigm and example above.
